analysis.title: GS Johnstone - GS TMT SPEC SALES: Nvdia beat & Raise; Software questions; Indra procurement questions; DSY hockey stick; US Equity Strategy 18 Nov 2026
key_insights: Nvidia reported a beat and raise with strong Vera Rubin execution. Management said the leadership transition has not disrupted customer or supplier relationships. Semis rallied in the US (Marvell, AMD) and in Asia (Samsung +2%, Hynix +4%).
The desk sees the print as near-term supportive for semis. Few expected a miss and the longer-term debate remains. Buyside expectations for FY2028 EPS were around $18, above the guide's roughly $17.

Nvidia is dialling back its role as financier of the AI buildout. The desk reads this as positive for Nvidia CDS and spreads, and negative for neoclouds that rely on residual guarantees or offtake support. Nebius and CoreWeave were still up about 10% after hours, and the desk says to watch their CDS.

Nvidia's financial commitments to customers and supply chain partners total $518bn, up from $366bn last quarter. Supply and capacity commitments ($390bn, largely memory) and datacenter leases ($74bn) account for most of the rise. Neocloud-related commitments total $32bn.

Nvidia says it will prioritise financing for projects with land, power, buildings and clear demand, and guarantees only take effect once projects are ready. This is positive for Nvidia's balance sheet but could make funding harder for leveraged neoclouds, widening the gap with investment-grade hyperscalers.

Gross margins are guided to bottom at 71-72% in January as memory costs rise, then settle at 72-73% in FY2028. CPU revenue is expected to more than double in FY2028, driven by agentic AI. The January-quarter guide assumes no China data-centre compute sales and includes an extra week.

AI credit stays in focus. Fed Governor Barr's November 16 Milan speech frames AI as a systemic financial risk, with the Fed mapping credit links, counterparty exposure and operational transmission channels tied to the buildout.

Software fell on the day, with IGV down 3% (Salesforce -9%, ServiceNow -6.5%, Workday -5.8%). The desk sees no new company-specific news. It attributes the move to multiple compression on the thesis that AI agents replace seats and erode pricing power, plus forced selling ahead of equity issuance.

The desk lists a cluster of software and IT outages and incidents: the Microsoft 365 global outage, an Apple outage after a faulty update, an NSA internal network outage, an emergency out-of-band Oracle patch and the Binance crypto heist. It cites Wired that there is no evidence they are related or caused by hackers. NSA later said its outage was tied to software updates.

SAP was weighed down by the resignation of its Chief Customer Officer, who is leaving to become IONOS CEO. Dassault Systemes (DSY) held a capital markets day that failed to inspire, because guidance implies a sharp hockey stick in growth over the next few years.

DSY's financial framework targets ARR growth accelerating from 7-8% at end-2026 to 10% by end-2029, 2029 revenue CAGR of about 8-9%, operating margin above 35% and diluted EPS of €1.80 (10% EPS CAGR). About 400bps of efficiencies fund roughly €250m of reinvestment, leaving 300bps of net margin expansion. The 2029 operating cash flow target of €2.5bn is 5% above the Street.

DSY plans to charge for Virtual Companions through usage-based tokens on top of existing seats. The open debate is whether this offsets falling token costs without cutting seat revenue. Management is optimistic on Life Sciences, saying Medidata is back to growth.

Indra faces new reputational and legal risk. Press reports an IGAE internal audit found the Ministry of Defence pre-selected Indra and EM&E for three contracts worth €2.348bn. Alleged irregularities include awards decided months before bids were invited and bidding windows as short as 14 days. The desk calls this the first public reporting of investigative findings.

Indra's exposure to the 29 November Spanish election is debated. A PP and VOX government would raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP from 2%, and the Indra CEO has already been named in anticipation of a change in government. Indra's favourable treatment under the current government could still leave it exposed.

Goldman's Ben Snider expects S&P 500 EPS growth to slow from about 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027, supporting a 17% rise to 8,700 at a multiple near 18x. 2028 is the larger uncertainty, with baseline EPS growth of +11% and a wide range of outcomes as AI capex decelerates and the market needs a handoff to AI monetisation.

Snider's preferred exposures are AI beneficiaries including hyperscalers, less disruptable physical business models, buyback aristocrats, secular growth, transports, energy infrastructure, healthcare and staples.

TrendForce expects NAND prices to start falling in Q2 2027 as YMTC expands, while DRAM ASPs hold through end-2027. HBM4 pricing is projected to rise from at least $2.05/Gb in 2026 to $3.00-$5.50/Gb in 2027. Nvidia's memory commitments drove the jump in its purchase commitments.

China's envoy warns that Dutch ASML export curbs threaten the EU-China trade thaw, while the Dutch resist the US MATCH Act. China is still about 30% of ASML prior-year revenue. Separately, new US proposals would restrict China's access to high-end AI chips and block imports of Chinese data center equipment.

The US market closed broadly heavier, with SPX below its 200-day moving average at 7344, after firmer retail sales and cyber-incident headlines. Asset managers were net sellers, driven by large-cap tech, and hedge fund flows were balanced. Nike fell 6% after being up 3% on investor skepticism of its 2031 guide.
Criteo is in play. Press suggests AppLovin is among companies in talks to buy it, after a joint approach from Vista Equity Partners and Quinti Capital in July 2026.
Isomorphic Labs raised $5bn in a Series C co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia, after a $2.1bn Series B in May. Valuation was not disclosed, though Bloomberg reported it was seeking $50bn.

market_movers.rationale: Beat and raise, FY2028 revenue growth guide lifted to about 75% from 70%, and a $150bn addition to the buyback. Stock +3% to +5% after hours. Export restrictions remain a risk.
Stock finished down 6% (from +3%) on its investor day as investors were deeply skeptical of the 2031 guide.
Siltronic upgraded to buy from hold at Berenberg (listed under Away From GS).
Moody's upgraded three USD subordinate hybrid instruments of Vodafone to Baa3 from Ba1, with a stable outlook.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term supportive after the Nvidia print, but few expected a miss and the longer-term debate remains.

The desk describes the selloff as multiple compression on the AI-replaces-seats thesis plus forced selling ahead of equity issuance, with no new company-specific news. This is a description of the move, not a rating.
Constructive on 2027, with S&P 500 EPS +18% and an 8,700 target. Prefers AI beneficiaries including hyperscalers, buyback aristocrats, transports, energy infrastructure, healthcare and staples.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reported results on 11/18 after the close. FY2028 revenue growth guidance was raised to around 75% from 70%, implying roughly $741bn of revenue and close to $17 of EPS against a Street estimate of $16 and buyside expectations of $18.
Nvidia January-quarter revenue guidance is $130bn ±3%, ahead of expectations. It includes an extra week and assumes no China data-centre compute sales.
Nvidia's Vera Rubin generated nearly $20bn of revenue in its first quarter. Gross margins are guided to bottom at 71-72% in January, then 72-73% in FY2028.
Nvidia's remaining buyback authorisation is around $227bn, and US trading commentary cites a $150bn addition to the buyback.
Dassault Systemes (DSY) held a capital markets day. It targets Q4 growth of 5-8% including acquisitions (in line), 2029 EPS of €1.80 and 2029 operating cash flow of €2.5bn, 5% above the Street.
Nike held an investor day and finished down 6% as investors were skeptical of its 2031 guide.

crypto_views: The Binance crypto heist is listed among recent technology and security incidents unsettling sentiment.
risk_factors: Export restrictions on Nvidia, and the January guide assumes no China data-centre compute sales.
Leveraged neoclouds that rely on Nvidia guarantees or offtake support face tighter funding as Nvidia becomes more selective.
AI credit and counterparty links are now framed as systemic financial risk by the Fed.
Software multiple compression on the AI-replaces-seats thesis and upcoming equity issuance.
Indra procurement irregularities could bring fraud and unlawful-decision allegations, rival challenges and European scrutiny of Article 346 national-security exemptions.
Indra's exposure to a change in Spanish government after the 29 November election.
DSY's growth plan relies on a back-end-loaded acceleration that investors must take on trust.
2028 EPS uncertainty as AI capex decelerates before AI monetisation arrives.
Escalating China tech restrictions and possible reciprocal measures against Dutch ASML curbs.
vol_and_positioning: US trading floor activity was a 3 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers finished net sellers, driven by large-cap tech, while hedge fund flows were balanced.
The SOX Index is described as being at an interesting point for chartists. No level is given in the text.
Software selling is partly forced selling by investors preparing for upcoming equity issuance.
geopolitical: New US proposals to restrict China's access to high-end AI chips, including renting Nvidia chips outside the US and obtaining processors through other countries.
Reuters report that the Trump administration plans to press ahead with efforts to block imports of Chinese data center equipment.
Chinese envoy warns Dutch ASML export curbs threaten the EU-China trade thaw. The Dutch resist the US MATCH Act, and Beijing signals possible reciprocal tech restrictions.
Spanish general election on 29 November, with a possible PP and VOX government that would raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP.
UK government Be Ready campaign urges people to stock up supplies for 72 hours, and panic buying of generators was reported in the US.
Suspected AI-assisted cyberattacks on South Korean financial institutions last month.
